Review: The best vehicle I drove under high-wind conditions.  Poor gas milage with an average of 14 mpg at a steady 65 to 75 mph and 800 lb load.  My Ford F150 under same conditions yielded 15.5 mpg.Build quality is very good.Design of truck is very good.Buy this truck if you need to haul a serious payload, otherwise get an F-150.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is a large, heavy duty, truck.  It is outstanding for hauling heavy lods or pulling heavy .    It is tough and reliable.  But it is hard to anuever in tight places and sometimes hard to park.  Turning radius is quite large.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I honestly don't know why anyone would consider buying anything else. Bought w/150,000 mi. Replaced the fuel sensor about 2 yrs ago. That's it..at 160,000 mi!! Change the oil and go. Why on earth Ford stopped building this motor is exactly the reason why buyers are abandoning their trucks in droves. If you buy a 6.0L or a 6.4L, you deserve what you get. You would do well to talk to diesel mechanics first. I'm going to upgrade soon and I guess that I'll have to go to the GMC Duramax, much as I hate to. Just a great, great motor in a great truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: As a truck goes this is a great vehicle. Never had a problem hauling or towing. I used this truck to commute with occasional towing of a camper and boat. By no means an abused or roughly treated vehicle. Before buying one be advised about the cost of owning a HD Ford. The ball joints have to be replaced every 30K at a cost of $1,000 here in New England. The brakes and rotors replaced at 35K...yup close to another grand. Tires, normal wear but they're about a thousand too. Also replaced the front locking hubs twice already...600 bucks each time. Oil changes are more costly too especially since takes 16 quarts of oil! Expect to pay about $1,000 annually for maintenance.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Ordered new in 1/2002. Been all over the USA with it, off road, snow and towed cars and trailers, never had any problems at all. Only thing that quit was the overdrive button recently. Brakes replaced at 100k! New tires 3 times including originals, but other than that just routine maintenance. Used Mobil 1 oil since new. Ride is a bit bouncy but then I have offroad and camper packages so its expected. Wish the back seat folded flat for better loading, and would prefer a real ashtray like the older models had. I get 16mpg hwy driving with cruise and at speed limit, also added air bags in rear for hauling camper and building materials. I expect to go another 100k miles no problem.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Bought it new. Wanted the 7.3 diesel before the 6.0's came out. Turned out that was the right move!  Got 13 to 17 mpg until about 45000 miles. Once past that mileage is 15.5+ in town and 21+ on the highway. Really a great truck! The only repairs have been, center link got sloppy, replaced it, Cam position sensor $30.00 part and 10 minutes to change, and cd changer went bad after 5 years and hard use. Got a replacement cd module that bolts into the radio in 5 minutes. So easy it suprised me.  No mechanical problems whatsoever, never dripped a drop of anything.  I think i'll keep it!

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 2WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I bought this truck used with 50,000 miles on it and in mint condition. I've owned a number of Ford trucks in the past including f-150s and f-250s and this one is the best of the bunch. It's an XLT with a long list of extras including the 6.8L v-10. All the interior options make for a nice enjoyable ride and that engine is fantastic. Endless acceleration and power.City driving gives about 10 mpg and highway is 15. This is driving with a lead foot.If the rpms are kept between 1500-2000 the mileage can be improved on. But, really, who buys a truck like this to drive like grandma?

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Bought in June of 2005, This F250 SD extended cab LB 4x4 has been excellent so far. It is the "true blue" color which looks awesome. Inside, captains chairs with a huge center console. There are more cupholders than seats, (5) seats. (6) cupholders.  Very easy to clean cloth. A/C thumbs up. Also very quiet, even with dual 4" straight pipes. 5.4L engine could use a little more power and the headlights could be brighter but truck is an excellent fun to drive vehicle, except in tight spots. Gas mileage with tonneau cover averages about 20 on highway, 8-12 in city. Braking power is enormous. Truck runs great with almost 61,000 miles. Only the trailer hitch rusted quite a bit but has not gotten to anything else.G

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: 7.3 litre diesel w/6-speed manual. The high pressure oil pumped leaked and needed to be replaced. The clutch master cylinder failed. The pass. window rattled when down. The tailgate lock, locks automatically. After the autopump sensor stops the flow of fuel to the tank, you can slowly pump another 6 gallons in the tank. The front rotors needed to be replaced or turned every 5,000 miles due to warping. This is a chronic and known problem with these vehicles. Worst of all there is EXCESSIVE driveline lash in the rear end/transmission/transfer case. It is VERY noticable between shifts and upon moderate acceleration. I wouldn't buy another Ford pickup.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 2WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: My F250 has the 7.3 Powerstroke. So many people say that these trucks aren't great for gas mileage, but obviously you aren't buying these for that purpose. However, spending the extra $5,000 for the diesel will pay for it itself. It gets far better mileage than the V10 or Triton, lasts longer, pulls better and will more than pay for itself when it comes down to resale value. Just look at the prices on used trucks with these 3 different motors.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have wanted an F-250 for a long time so I finally got one. It is a great truck! I got the PowerStroke diesel. The truck is very powerful. Of course the diesel is probably not as quick as the V-10, but it is quite surprising for a diesel. I love the fact that it has front and rear solid axles for strength and durability. While everyone else is going to independent suspension to improve ride and handling,I am glad that Ford has not done that on the Superduty. The ride of this truck is EXCELLENT for a truck! Ford really did it right.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Ford has done a great job with all aspects of this truck. Even the fuel economy is better than you would think but not great, between 12 and 13 on my 5.4 V-8.

Review: great truck, best in class

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 2WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Very nice tough truck

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: Nice truck, but a gas hog.
Review: I opted for the 4x4 extended cab and short bed. Only negatives are fuel efficency and the captains chairs aren't as comfortable as the bench seat in my '93 F-150 I owned previously. Also, cab steps are a must for getting in and out easily. Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XL 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: Once it gets started it's a blast

Right now this thing has turned into a money pit, as i speak it sits dead again on my driveway, and yes it is plugged in, it's always plugged in

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have had this truck now for 5 years. i have gone cross country and and mudding just about any thing you can think of. The reason i bout this truck is because my friends and the 03 and 04 F-250 diesil 6L something but it was garbage. I have never done anything but lift it, oil change, and new tires other wise all the thinds i have done it runs brand new like the day i bought it. It has so much power and the Turbo makes it sound amazing. My best friend has a Dodge Ram 1500 diesil and i can go so many more places faster and eaiser. i would buy this truck agian and not a newer one the 1999-2002 is the year u want trust me!

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Pulled my 30' 5th wheel with no problems although my MPG dropped by half. I found that if I hauled any load without the "cruise control", I had better milage. The cruise worked well, it would just eat too much fuel, especially through hilly country. I have just over 100 000 kms (Can) & have gone through 2 alternaters (1 at 29000 & 2nd at 69000) already. I did install a set of Pia lights on my "kangaroo bumper" in 2003, not sure if this is the problem or not. Warrenty covered everything including both batteries. These were the only serious issues. I love it & take really good care of it. I hope to get 400 000kms more. I am happy with MPG getting over 700kms/tank (HW) while driving 100-110kmh.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: 5.4l gas gets me 10 mpg and it was sort of itching my hide but gas has come way down. The good thing is even if I am hauling 4k trailer load behind me, I still get 10 mpg. Don't know why. I know this truck does not feel like I am hauling anything, and the 4X4 feature got me unstuck two times at the city dump when it was storming both times. My Chevy 1500 gets about 22 mpg but I drive my F250 and the Chevy sits there. Maybe I will give it to my 16 year old son. The F250 is a power house getting on the interstate or highway. I have no problem getting up to 65, even pulling a 4k load. This is with a 5.4 gas engine.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: No Wonder SuperDuty Outsells Them All !
Review: The 7.3L Powerstroke is an excellent "tried & true" diesel.I put a K&N air kit on & it roars and takes off like a bullet.Rides & drives better than mom's Cadillac. Though it  weighs in @ 7,100 lbs., the 20mpg I get on the road is amazing.  I have tested all the other makes.  The fit & finish of Ford trucks is vastly superior to the cheap look & feel of the Chevy/GMC. The Super Duty overall design is well planned. I like the fact that the Super Duty is THE ONLY 3/4 ton truck designed & built as such with its own special heavy duty frame. Chevy/GMC/Ram simply install higher spring rates in their 1/2 tons and call it a "heavy duty".

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: My Ford F250 has been rode hard and putaway wet.  I have already put 60,000mile on in the first two years and I'venever had a days problem with it.  I doa lot of  off roading, beach driving,towning and highway driving.  I wish allof Fords vechicles were this well built.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: in the shop more than on the road
Review: A new f250 with lots of repairs is unacceptable.Only 22000 miles and have had new rotors,brakes, front springs and soon tires dues too improper front end problems.Must have been a Friday or Monday built truck. Now have a vibration, rattle under the truck to take in next week. I hope Ford Motor Co. reads this because they have not cared so far. I've had the truck in the shop for close too 2 weeks total time. I use this truck for work and buy new every 2 years too prevent down time, which costs me MONEY.Not sure where I'll buy next, but I know this truck is gone at 36000 mi.THis is not the dealers fault. Poorly made truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This truck replaced my 99.5 SD SC PSD

column1: and there is a world of difference
between the two.  The 02 is much
quieter and refined with major emphasis
on NVH dampening.  I added a Superchip
1700 programmer and this truck is

the cruise set on 80.  The speed
limiter is gone now and this truck with
3.73 does 117 mph on the GPS(not on
public roads of course)!  I can't wait
to see what the 03 does with 6.0 and
5spd auto.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

diesel rules!  Should have gotten
limited slip.  Need to plan approach
to parking lots (very large turning

bar.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

column1: None have been as well built as this
truck.  I compared it to the Chevy
2500HD Diesel.(ha ha)  This is a real
truck.  It has everything I was looking

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Got the V10 cause I'm a power freak and I couldn't pass up the 400lb torque figures. Thought I could live with the gas mileage and I guess I'll have to. 13.5 on hiway 9.5 to 11 around town. It is kinda fun to burn rubber in a vehicle this big though. I basicly bought this as a family car to replace my old Suburban. The only thing I'm missing is the 3rd seat and I saved about 7k over a similarly equipped Suburban. Plus I can haul bicycles and stuff easier now. Put a lockable tool box on it, after market, that serves as a trunk.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: The Ford Super Duty is the best truck I've ever driven. Right now it's getting 19 miles per gallon and for a truck this big, which haul or tow almost anything, that's incredible. I highly recommend the truck and Borman ford here in Las Cruces, NM. They have treated me great!!!

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I am 5'2 120lbs, not exactly what you expect to see jumping out of this big truck.  I thought my husband was crazy, but I test drove it and fell in love.  I will never own another kind of vehicle.  I can fit 2 car seats, 3adults, and a 12 year old.  I had a bachlorette party of 10 women (not recommended and definitely not legal).  It's a car and a truck combined. Great stereo, AC, and lots of cup holders (the important stuff). Big yet easy to drive. I look great driving it.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: The best truck on the market

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: the four wheel drive totally kicks

column1: ass. great for camping and hunting.
very roomy.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: The power and the feeling of power that this truck transmits is awesome. The feeling of being safe is equally as awesome. Very comfortable, huge cabin, impressive legroom space in the back seats (as much as the front). I love this truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: A True Truck - Not a Grocery Cart
Review: This is my second F-250 with the V-10. I owned a 5 speed(extended cab), and the new crew cab this time I got with the automatic which works as well, and has no fuel mpg difference, and I m not shifting spilling my coffee. I've driven this truck pulling a heavy enclosed cargo trailer, and have not had any mechanical failure.  Minor problems appeared early in ownership, and covered by dealer under warranty. If you need a Real Truck, not a Grocery Cart or Kid Transporter - the superduty is hard to beat by other manufacturers.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 2WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I bought my Truck in January.  I used to have a GMC yukon.  The Ford is awesome.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 2WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: SO FAR I AM VERY PLEASED WITH MY TRUCK.  THE V-10 HAS MORE THAN ENOUGH POWER FOR ME.  STYLE AND LOOKS WISE, THE TRUCK IS A REAL HEAD TURNER.  MY ONLY COMPLAINT WOULD BE THE SEATS.  I CAN NOT GET COMFORTABLE YET.  AFTER AN HOUR OF DRIVING, MY LOWER BACK HURTS.  STILL TRYING TO REMEDY THAT.

Vehicle_Title: 2002 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Quite simply, the best pickup I've ever owned.  More power than I expected with a great interior to boot.  Far superior to the last Ford crew-cab I had.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab XLT 2dr Regular Cab 4WD LB
Review: Awesome truck. Rides nice for a heavy truck. Stiff on the road. Nice for towing and awesome gas mileage  for such a big truck

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab XL 2dr Regular Cab 4WD LB
Review: This is my son's truck and I love to drive it. Its awesome, 6 speed manual transmission, 4-Wheel drive, its one Tough truck. It gets around 18 mpg. And its used for work, he is always pulling something with it. He puts that truck through a test daily. Even my brother who is a mechanic loves the truck, he said that truck has some pulling power.This truck has even pulled a Dodge backwards that had a Cummins in it.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab XLT 2dr Regular Cab LB
Review: is great truck to own very reliable

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab LB
1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XL 4dr Extended Cab LB
1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XL 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: I bought this truck brand new in 1999 I pulled a 30 foot travel trailer from Louisville Kentucky to California several times averaging 16 - 18 miles per gallon empty average 22 - 24 miles/gallon I had to replace the starter alternator minor repairs best truck I ever owned 7.3 is great motor

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab SB
Review: I bought mine to tow my travel trailer. I recently changed the rear end to 430 limited slip and love the change for towing. At 96K I needed to repair the exhaust manifold bolts which was a major pain. Wheel bearings also don't last very long.  Overall I love the truck.  Mine is a 2WD version with the V10.  It is a towing beast!

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab 4WD SB
Review: My Super Duty reached it's 10th B day in May. Its easy to rate a vehicle when its a year or two old with a few miles on it. My truck just passed 270k and it still looks better than any other 3 or 4 year old truck. It has pulled loads to 30k over trips of 6000 miles in mountains. Mileage never less than 16 - 20 empty and never added a qt of oil between changes of 5000 miles. This with the truck living mostly in Minnesota's salt and snow. This truck has never let me down even in the 9 winters with sub zero temps. To date the only items replaced were the normal consumables like brakes, wheel bearings, etc. Teh engine still runs like new teh tranny is solid and the body shows no rust.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab 4WD SB
Review_Title: I can't believe its a FORD!!!!!
Review: i bought this truck a month ago. The original owner purchased it new in 1999. It have 144,000 miles and runs perfect. Fuel economy it great i have a 2006 honda ridgeline and the 7.3 powerstroke gets better fuel mileage. Mixed city and highway i get 18-20.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab Lariat 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: Ford knows how to make a pulling truck although they give up decent fuel economy in the process. My V10 gets about 11 mpg with the 4.30 gears. The truck is very reliable but it does use a quart of oil between changes. The transmission is bullet proof with regular fluid changes. Previous comments were correct, you can't go anywhere other than on pavement without 4x4 due to the weight.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab Lariat 4dr Extended Cab 4WD LB
Review: I purchased my 1999 in 2005 for about $15,000 with about 45,000 miles on it, and it had a 5th wheel hitch and normal receiver hitch already on it.  Mine is the Lariat with 4WD, and full 8' bed, with the V-10 gasoline.  Primary use was to ocasionaly pull a boat with the normal hitch or horse trailer with the 5th wheel.  Does a very good job pulling either one! Gas mileage is poor, but with the big V-10 you should expect that.  I only get about 10-11 mpg highway when not pulling, and with a heavy horse trailer loaded it drops down to the 8 mpg range on highway.  It seats 5 with no issues and is comfortable.  You do have to "climb up" into it - and ride is stiff when not loaded or pulling.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab 4WD LB
Review_Title: '99 F-250 X-Cab XLT 4x4 long box w/ V10
Review: This is one GREAT truck - sharp looking and tons of power.  That V10 just screams - NO problems hauling a loaded stock trailer up hills doing 60.  Mileage is better than expected at ~16 mpg.  Interior is nicer than my living room - and cleaner!  Built solid and drives solid.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab Lariat 4dr Extended Cab 4WD SB
Review_Title: a man's truck that  women like to drive
Review: It's been the best truck we have ever own of all of them (dodge,chevy,ford) we bought it to pull a 34' 5th wheel trailer (did great). only dislike is it's too front heavy with the diesel to drive on the beach. so we're down sizing to a smaller truck

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XL 4dr Extended Cab 4WD LB
Review: this is alot of truck for the buck, it sure does drive nice and has the capacity to perform!

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab Lariat 4dr Extended Cab 4WD LB
Review_Title: Make Sure You Need A Real Truck!
Review: Very capable truck for hauling and towing.  Ride is rough due to leaf spring suspension and steering feel is numb.  If you don't need 3/4-1 ton capacity, you will be happier with the ride, performance and comfort of an 150.  Overall gas mileage has been excellent for a truck this size with a range of 11-14 mpg.  I recommend not getting the 4.3 gears unless you tow heavy.  3.73s are a better all around choice.  (I've got the 4.3s.)  I'd steer clear of the manual trans as they are noisey and slow shifting.  (Yes, I've got one.)

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab Lariat 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review_Title: F250 Larait - All around great truck
Review: I bought this truck with 35,000 miles on it and I have never had a any trouble with it whatsoever. This truck is very stable on the highway. I use this truck both as an off road and highway vehicle. I have a farm which makes it necessary to get this truck in a soft muddy barn yard as well as the fields using 4WD. I also have pulled heavy fertilizer spreaders up steep grades with this truck on the highway. The Triton engine performed far better than I expected. The fuel compsupmtion is a little high at about 12 to 15 mpg, but, with this big engine that's to be expected. I would buy this truck again in a heartbeat!

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: Just bought 3 days ago and have added

column1: 100 miles to the odometer (almost to
40K now).  Has 5.4 with a manual
trans.  Trans has problem with second
gear that seems to be a ford trait
(had same problems in a 76 and 79).
Double clutching gets rid of the grind
problem.  Wife enjoys the ride and
drive.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: This is the last truck I will ever own, because I will never need another one. In fact, I'll likely pass it and the RV it pulls down to my children.I am absolutely pleased with its performance, reliability and capability. Although initial cost is pretty high for the diesel, operating costs are not that great, and the added versatility and towing capacity make up for it. This truck does everything I need it to do.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XL 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: I bought used at 106K miles but truck was very clean. Now have 118K and no problems so far. Very nice to drive but be careful when you sip your coffee! Very solid ride but seats are excellent for comfort. Used as a daily commuter and feel safe in traffic. The transmission bangs into each gear with nice positive feel. The 5.4 engine has a rap when starting cold and startled me first few times but was told by other owners theirs make same noise. Whatever it is, the performance is not affected and it does disappear within minutes. Overall, I love the truck and would recommend without question.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab 4WD SB
Review: Great truck.  Fun to drive, except parking in some parking lots.  No problems yet.  Don't work it very hard, I just wanted a durable truck.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XL 4dr Extended Cab LB
Review: I bought my 5.4 with 98k miles and

column1: have close to 117K after 8 months.
Used as a daily driver and love the
firm ride and safety. No problems so
far and seems very solid. The 14mpg
is a little rough but worth the tradeoff.
Pulls an 18 ft loaded car trailer with
ease. I have the xtended cab/longbed
so can be a mother in the turning
radius dept. Went thru a Taco Bell
drive thru and had to drive over the
curb and into the flowers when

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Extended Cab XLT 4dr Extended Cab SB
Review: great truck for pulling my 5th wheel RV

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab SB
Review_Title: Amazing truck but has it's flaws.
Review: Pros: Super reliable: 220k on mine and all it's needed is 2 alternators and a set a glow plugs. Super powerful: Hits 90mph easily but has a Governor at 92. Neutral: Gas mileage: Horrible when going slow or stop and go. Got 5mpg in some areas before. BUT, I get 18-20 on the Hwy and Freeways and ~15 when pulling a large trailer which is amazing considering how big and powerful the vehicle is.Cons: Lots of little stuff. Bad stereo, AC works but needs Freon and doesn't have recirculating air, power locks broke, electric seat adjuster barely works, tires are too small for the engine so flats and tire ware can be an issue, bad traction when not in 4x4 but it's only an issue during snow or when off roading.Summary: Everything that matters works amazingly and is super reliable but it does have many small problems.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB
Review: my truck has 129,000 and no problems till now blew a spark plug out of the head . not to exspensive $213.00 for aspark plug and a coil and a sleeve simular to a helix coil, but no drilling involed just insert and spread took less than 2 hours truck is a beast. ford screwed us on the gas but 18 on the freeway is'nt bad the harley makes up for the winter gas i spend !!! Parking sucks in a crowded place !

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB
Review: Beware of Ford Diesel 7.3, bad fuel economy, hard to start, bad electronic, bad transmission, mechanics' nightmare. Turning radius is very bad.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab SB
Review: Bought my F250 new have 150K on it and not a problem one with the 7.3L diesel. Pull a 34' 5th wheel with it and it does not skip a beat.. Fuel economy is good for a truck of this size..16-17 city --21-23 hyway.. pulling I get between 12 and 14 MPG. Better than my gas truck use to get.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: We bought the truck with 150,000 miles on it. We have since then put another 10,000 miles on it and it still runs like a champ. 4x4 works amazing!  We love it! The only thing is that you need to change your spark plugs at about every 50k to ensure that they won't blow out of the head. That's expensive.  Computer console has a short and does not work. All in all love the truck and will not trade for a long long time.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: I have had a very good experiance with my Ford F-350 Superduty 7.3 liter diesel. It has a full box and 4 doors making it very long, but for hauling 5th wheel trailers it works flawlessly. Empty I get 18 mpg; with a 15,000 lb. trailer 10 mpg; with a 30,000 lb. trailer 5-7 mpg (yes we have pulled 30k lb. trailer several times, once even a truck plus trailer weight of about 39,000 lb.). One problem with its own weight being almost 8,000 lb. empty, if you ever leave solid road surfaces you will need 4WD. All around though I would say it is an amazing truck that redefined the pick-up-truck.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB
Review: Great Truck, value, tough.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab SB
Review: Great truck needs larger front brakes

column1: and a large fuel tank.   Awesome truck
with plenty of power.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab SB
Review: Great truck, the only complaint is 10mpg. I knew what I was getting into when I bought the nice and quiet V10, and added front and rear replacement bumpers, toolbox and 35" BFG mud tires. Pulls trailers "ok", not to good on hills. But overall is a great and reliable truck.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review_Title: For a BIG truck... can't beat it!
Review: It pulls, climbs and gets you there safely.  Other trucks try, this one does.  The diesel engine is just being broke in at 100,000 miles.  Very low maintanance if you service it regularly.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: Great truck. fun to drive, very reliable Has 120000 miles and runs like new.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: This thing with the 7.3 PowerStroke is a monster!  It has the manual 6 speed trans, and can climb steep grades pulling a 6500lb camper...at 65MPH in 4th...passing other vehicles!  The crew cab carries 5 comfortable, 6 in a crunch (manual trans, remember?).  Without a load, it gets 16-17 MPG city, and 18-19 on the road at 65-70 MPH.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: I just traded it in with 52350 miles. It had the Powerstroke, auto. The ONLY thing that ever went wrong was an alternator failure right at 50,000 miles.  It turns out that the alternator bearings were out of spec from the beginning and it was wearing out from day 1.  $160 later, I had it running.  Other than that, it was powerful, economical to drive, and very reliable.  I liked it well enough that I bought a 2003 just about like it!

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB
Review: This truck must have running boards.

column1: with proper modifications you can get
26 mpg.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab LB
Review: Pull, push, haul or whatever you want to do with anything you want to do it with.  DO IT WITH A F250 SD.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab LB
Review: Drove Ford Chevy & Dodge.  Dodge 4x4 V8: no crew cab, rough idle, mushy cornering.  Chevy: no 4 wheel disks, lower apparent build quality especially interior fit & finish.  Stiff twin I beam front suspension on the 2x4 corners best.  12~13 MPG commuting, to 8 MPG ave with 11,000+ pound slide-in camper rig.   Added FORD & aftermarket anti-sway bars, air springs & 110 PSI Goodyear steel carcas tires on the single rear wheels to kill over-steer.  Rates 8800 pounds max, but run a scale-verified 11,000+ pounds regularly, + 2 motorcycles on a front rack into dual Draw-Tite and Warn front-end receiver hitches.

Vehicle_Title: 1999 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB
Review: Can't go wrong ith  the power stroke

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab XL 2dr Regular Cab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I use this vehicle to tow daily and it is always up for the task at hand it also has no problem plowing and with 2500lbs in the bed. Also has no problem with a loaded bed  while towing my 7,000lb loaded trailer. gas mileage is not the greatest but when hauling a lot that's a given. I believe the engine is powerful enough ( I have the 5.4) but theres always room for improvement. I expect 10 years of hard work from this vehicle

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XL 4dr SuperCab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XLT 4dr SuperCab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I had the 5.4L V8, auto, extended cab with long bed.The truck had plenty of power.I used it to tow a 23 foot camper.It barely fit into my garage.It rode well on the highway and you could't mess up the outside.The interior was pretty plain but held up pretty well.It was my family truck but the person before me used it as a work truck only.Sucked fuel.There was a carbon canister that filtered the fumes from the gas tank that clogged.It was a couple hundred dollar fix.So I just disconnected it myself.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XLT 4dr SuperCab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I purchased this truck as an 07 leftover and got a great deal that was hard to pass up. I absolutely love it. It's a rugged yet stylish truck with the chrome package.  Perfect to tow 34ft camper, boats and snow-removal.  Pure power is all it has to offer it will jolt you back into your seat if you hammer it of the line, its like a jet.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XL 4dr SuperCab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: 54 miles and found on road dead
Review: i purchased this vehicle and happily drove it for two and one half hours before it would not start.  i called for the emergency roadside service only to be disappointed by the lack of service after waiting for a tow for almost two hours in 88 degree heat in the evening. I called a private tow company which arrived in 13 minutes to tow my new $32,831.61 truck to my home (the dealer was closed). This is the new 6 liter diesel with automatic transmission.  I have owned many new Fords but we may have to get this one painted yellow.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty King Ranch
Review: This is my first Ford Truck and I am very happy with it.  I bought it to pull my 8000 LB travel trailer and it pull it with ease.  I have a 5.4 gas engine and it is more than powerful enough.  It goes up steep grade pulling my trailer with ease and the braking power is more than enough coming down the steep grades.  I am hoping to get many years of reliable service from this truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is the first Ford truck I've ever owned. I must say I got the top of the line with this truck. I have the F250 Harley Davidson in Dark Stone color. I feel that it looks second to none out there. After I bought it I read reviews on the Powerstroke. I realize you should research first! I have not had any problems with my Powerstroke. I have it serviced as required and driven 73,000 miles with pure pleasure.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I like the toughness of this truck!  Heavy duty in every aspect!  It's quiet, no road noise and the seating is comfortable.  The axles are built Ford tough and look like they will last forever.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: The 6.0 Powerstroke tows heavy equipment like it is empty. The torque is exceptional and the automatic transmission is geared perfectly whether loaded or empty. The brakes are very responsive unlike the spongecake type of the Chevy I replaced. My vote would be Cummins (Dodge) first, Ford second and the Duramax should actually be used for boat anchors. I went Ford because the Dodge people can't build a chassis dependable to go with their engine.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: A real Truck...not a wannabe toy truck!
Review: This is my 2nd Ford Diesel Super Duty; my 2004 was trouble free for the 60,000 miles I had it. This new one is still the champ when it comes to towing, smooth as the Super Chief locomotive pulling a long line of freight cars up the "Grape Vine!" I agree that Ford needs to add sat radio and Nav units, but I already own both and transfered them from old truck to new. Comfortable cab, good controls, nice radio, power everything. Once my other PSD was broken in I got a consistent 22 mpg, towing was 16-18 with a medium size fifth wheel. This truck, being a long bed instead of shorty, has 10 gallons more fuel capacity, which I like.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: My Lariat FX4 Powerstroke diesel has exceeded my expectations with regards to power and towing ability.  I tow a 25+5 tandem axle gooseneck trailer and a 75 hp John Deere with implements and you would never know it's back there without looking in the mirror.  I also like the big rig styling of the Fords vs the smaller looking Chevys. The built in trailer braking system and 4 aux switches are a plus. With the 18" wheels it really sits up high and has good ground clearance. I agree with earlier post re: XM and Nav, not to mention no DVD option.  I was a bit hesitant with the new style coming out in '08 but the old style looks better than the competition to me.  Overall I could not be happier.

Vehicle_Title: 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: My $51,000.00 King Ranch was not available with the options that you would expect on a vehicle in this price range. You cannot get a navigation system in a vehicle we use to travel and tow a trailer. XM or Sirius radio are also not available in the F250. My ski boat and Harley both have satellite radio but not a $50K Ford. The Harley even has a nav system. WAKE UP FORD!

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab Lariat 4dr SuperCab SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Model selection feature on this site is messed up.My 2009 6.4L has 86,000 miles on it.On recenttrip pulling 5th wheel the engine goes into power de-rate (limp) mode and check engine light comes on.8 hour trip took 10 and I was sometimes only able to make 40 mph on interstate.Same deal on trip home (wasn't away long enough to have problem diagnosed and repaired).My dealership determined it was a pcv on fuel pump sticking.Had to replace entire fuel pump and it required cab removal!About $2800 total.Labor alone for cab removal and replacement is about 10 hours.Why on earth design a vehicle that requires cab removal for simple replacement of a critical part?

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XL 4dr SuperCab 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Ok this is my story. My first truck was a 2008 f250 5.4 cc the windshild had a bad leak and water got into the drivers side dash the truck developed some electricial problems so the dealership had to buy it back as a lemon. Thinking this was a fluke I bought another f250 sd cc 5.4 v8 two months later the windshild wipers would not turn off. The dealership told me it was a bad wiper motor. The gas mileage is bad at only 13mpg average. But hay you dont buy a big truck to worry about gas you buy it to haul pull whatever.The truck with the 5.4 is not a power house. I pull a 28ft travel trailer the truck has no problem susspenion wise but the 5.4 realy lacks the pulling power almost scarey

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Bought this truck new for pulling a 31 ft. camper and have loved every mile. Pulling power is excellent and gets decent MPG for a large crew cab. I have had the truck for 5 years and no issues. I had one recall but that was for the tires. I now have 43,000 miles on it and do not plan on getting rid of it any time soon. Did I tell you the pulling power is amazing!

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: 09 F250 6.4 kicked code during a trip to Galveston(350 m from home). Auto parts store 4 reset because it was in constant regen. Recorded code and took into dealer. Had truck two days, told nothing they could do because code was not in computer (35K miles). Asked "what happens if it does this again" service manager told me "just don't drive to far from the dealer and bring it in next time".Both batts dead (37k). Noticed slight drip of coolant (46k miles).Dealer: both radiator hoses bad and needed replaced.$683.Not covered by warranty.Took to local shop.Determined bad o ring in the upper hose only (is covered by warranty).New hose ebay $44.$50 for local shop. No more Ford 4 me.

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Overall, this truck has performed well.  However, at 6,400 miles the truck left me stranded on the side of the road at 4 a.m.  "Miles to Empty" message center was reading 46 miles to empty (light had just illuminated 4 miles earlier) and truck lost power and died.  Towed to Ford dealer.  Had to pay over $150 in diagnostics because it was out of fuel.  Ford will not acknowledge anything wrong with miles to empty calculator and was told to keep fuel tank 1/2 fuel to prevent problem.  Ford customer svc was not helpful and refused to admit anything was wrong with the truck.  Ford service tech admitted he's seen this before and Ford has a serious problem with these units.  Last Ford purchase.

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XLT 4dr Crew Cab SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is one very srong pulling truck. nice ride,looks great,Love that turbo feel and sound. Make's almost any pulling job seem like it isnt even there. I average 17.0 mpg 65mph. 10,000 mile's on it now.

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This 6.4L diesel F-250 is my fourth Ford deisel ( 2 - 7.3L's and one 6.0L ) and it seems to be the best engine design yet - had a slight fuel problem with the 6.0L.  The 6.4L has plenty of power and the truck rides extremely well. Mileage is lousy, only 13 - 14 mpg( 4WD hurts )but the trade off in power and safety and comfort are worth it. Especially like the navigation system, Sync, power folding mirrors, and interior roominess. Wife loves the heated leather seats. The tailgate step is great as are the 6" cab steps in the chrome pkge. I would HIGHLY recommend getting the electic auxillary cab heater ( one of the only options I passed up ), because of the increased cooling system capacity. HAPPY

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: It was time to trade out of my 92 F250. It gave me good service for 18 Years. This new one is my third truck. If this one gives me as good of service as the previous two fords, I will be happy. This is my first diesel. I pull a 30 foot 5th wheel. Looking forward to the power of the diesel.  So far I love the truck. The ride and comfort inside are great. Still learning how to use all the conveniences. The color (Red) with the chrome package is a real eye pleaser. It has most of the bells and whistles. I love the tailgate step and folding mirrors. Makes it easy to get int he garage. Was worried it would not fit but it does. I could not ask for more at this time.

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab XL 4dr Crew Cab SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I get 18 in the country and 21 on the highway in my 2009 ford diesel f250.I get 14 pulling a 13000 lbs hay trailer and pulls it easy.

Vehicle_Title: 2009 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Hi, since the first week of december I have this truck and I don't have any problems. MSRP 62k got all. I got a 29' (9000L) and you don't even realize is back. Gas mileage is 14mpg average on 6.4L diesel but is a big truck. No complains

Vehicle_Title: 2013 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab XL 4dr SuperCab 4WD LB (6.2L 8cyl 6A)
Review: Anyone having trouble with the middle seat? It doesn't go back but sits almost straight up. Though it folds down and becomes a central console with a place for cups, when it's up, it only has one position, and that's almost straight up. Who could sit like that? I would like to remove it or be able to tilt it back. It's called a 40/20/40 seat.

Vehicle_Title: 2013 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab Lariat 4dr Crew Cab 4WD SB (6.2L 8cyl 6A)
Review: Poor gas mileage but turns many heads!!! It’s a must have, gas is only 2.50!!!!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I bought this truck cause my 84 was so tough.This one is junk.Front end speed wobbles if you hit a bump at highway speeds dealer has tried to fix "NOT".5 power steering pumps and one gearbox. Yes it will lock up on you. If you drive a lot of dirt roads the Evap sys will suck dirt inand dispose of it in your gas tank "Yippi'Clogging fuel filters. Why cause the inlet is by the back wheels and the dirt causes the sylinoid to stick open.That is the check gas cap you keep seeing. Hyper sensitive electric gas pedalmake this truck hard to drive slow. Side window scratch just from rolling them up and down. Don't put anything in the bed cause it will dent.Plows great though.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Bought used with only 11000 miles. Now has 36864 on it. Bounces and shakes uncontrolable after hit bumps. Cost $795 to fix rear brakes after they seized up for no reason. Others I've talked with had same problems. Only buy if needing 3/4 ton or large truck. Otherwise I'd stick with Toyota or Nissan.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: V8 Auto: Good truck, but weak points.
Review: I bought this truck new before moving from TX to NY, and for long distance driving with a trailer this truck was fantastic. The 5.4 V8 is adequate but could be stronger.  At 22k I had to have a front bearing replaced due to water incursion, and while backing out of an icy driveway spinning tires, the xmsn had an internal failure that holed the xmsn case, and so at 27k back to Ford for warranty service again.  I'm afraid of further problems when the warranty runs out so I've decided to trade the truck in.  Overall, this is a top-notch hauling vehicle and great to drive on the long roads, but if you expect to use it for serious farm work or anything off pavement, you'll be disappointed.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I love this truck.  The fuel economy is not the best, but otherwise this truck does everything I need it to and more.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Replaced a '90 F150 which I also purchased new and was a mechanical nightmare. Swore I was never going to but another Ford truck ... oh well! My new F250 is a bare bones model that I sought long and hard for.  It is a pig on gas (11.5 mpg local) but so was the previous 5.8 that had nowhere near the power. No problems so far. Rear tires spin easily and sometimes need 4x4 to start out. Probably due to no load condition & 60 psi in the tires.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XL 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have only 3,000 miles on my truck and have had unintended acceleration four times. One of the four occured when the dealer tech was servicing. No engine lights or indicators to warn of computer listed errors. Motor revs from idle to 3,000 rpm without warning.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: My new Ford F-250 4X4 XLT has met all the requirements I wanted except mileage. My 1977 F-250 4X4 XL only gave 11 mpg so this one giving 14 mpg is much better, but I had hoped for better than 17 mpg. This is still one well built truck for the money.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Regular Cab 2dr Regular Cab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Although not broken in yet, out of 8 new Ford trucks, this is the worst one for gas mileage. Only 9 mpg. Truck has manual hubs and would not stay in 4WD.  A new shift assembly had to be installed with less than 1,000 miles on it. Very hard to steer in 4WD when trying to make a sharp turn in reverse. Sometimes the wheels won't move at all. The truck has 17" wheels and wide tires. The wide tires make the truck more difficult to handle when driving on snow covered roads. Power windows do not work in cold weather.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I drive my father's 2005 f250 4x4. The truck is incredibly rugged and powerful, 4x4 kicks ass! It plows snow with ease, tows a trailer like it's not even there, and is, in my opinion, pretty fast for it's size. The ford is definitely more of a work truck, but it still takes off and sounds awesome under heavy throttle. Always fires right up as it should on those 10 degree days in NH. I can't really think of any problems we've had with it, other than some brake issues caused by sitting too much.. Overall great vehicle I love it! But just remember it ain't no Prius, she is very thirsty!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I had a 2005 F-250 4x4 diesel that was towed out of my garage 7 weeks after buying it for electrical issues. By the beginning of 2009 it had been towed a total of about 7 times to the dealer for not starting, once was right after Ford put THEIR own batteries in it, thinking that would "fix" the issue since they believe it was the Walmart batteries that were killing the engine (even though it didn't come off the lot with Walmart batteries).

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I guess I'm the lucky one. In almost 6 years of towing I had vacuum pump go out that controlled the AC flow and a tubo hose blew off. We pull a 12,000 lb. 5th wheel from Florida to the Colorado Rockies each summer and the Powerstroke Diesel is an animal.  It's almost fun to pull the big passes in the mountains as well as using tow command coming down.  This engine is made to pull!  After the warranty expired I did an EGR delete.  This has been a major weak link with the '04 and '05 Powerstroke.  The last time I had service the report was the brakes, tie rods,and suspension are fine.  I had the computer reset to current Ford specs and drive, not towing, with a tonneau cover and get 18 mpg hwy

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I was traveling on the I 280 south freeway with my daughter to a soccer tournament in my 2005 F250 4x4 super duty truck. We were in cruise control going approx 55 mph. We drove over what I believe was a large expansion joint on the freeway. Immediately after we traveled over joint, the vehicle start to violently shake and vibrate. After a tense moment of complete terror as the vehicle became extremely difficult to control and continued to shake violently we came to a unsafe stop on the freeway. After the complete stop, I immediately had to speed up again to prevent being rear-ended in the middle of the freeway. This vehicle is extremely dangerous and needs to be removed from the road.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is by far the worst vehicle I have ever owned. It has been in the shop multiple times for suspension and mechanical problems. In 26,000 miles I have done had the steering gear box, replaced shocks, center drag link, steering stabilizer, all to no avail. The truck still has many problems that 3 Ford dealerships can't fix. At speeds of 60-70 mph if I hit a bump in the road the front end shakes so violently I have almost lost control on many occasions. It is a dangerous truck. It's stiff, it's rough. I personally hate it. This is definitely my last Ford purchase

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Drives great, tows and has enough power. However- nothing but problems with the Turbo Diesel. Had it 2 1/2 years, and in that time it has had major engine problems at least 3 times.  The Turbo went out. The "viens" in the diesel colapsed. The # 6 injector failed completely while on a trip, towing a trailer. Had to get it towed from the "middle of nowhere" to the dealer to fix. Under warranty, had a deductable of $100.00. After that, they covered the cost. BUT that did not cover the tow, and it did not instill any confidence for our next trip.  Not sure, but if one more thing happens, it's gonna get traded in for a Dodge. Not at all happy with the diesel engine's reliability.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Had several F150s but needed something to pull my 30ft RV in the Colorado mountains. Scored a 2005 SD, SC, Lariat, FX4 LB w/33K. This is an awesome truck. 6.0L powerstroke is incredible. The truck commands the road and most nearby traffic. It's loaded with just about every option and very comfortable. Leather is top quality, roomy, eye appealing inside and out. Handles well for being as big as it is. Have only had it a short time and already getting compliments. Liked the 2005 model changes to the grill best so went with that year. Suits me just fine. If it's like my other Fords, I'll get years of reliable service.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I use this truck for hauling a pickup camper that weighs about 4000 lbs. This unit works perfectly, Lots of power, easy to handle and just a great vehicle.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: Loved it till I owned it
Review: I love the exterior, looks great. Interior was nice, but for a taller guy in the back the extended cab doesn't have all that much room. Hauling capacity is great. In the cold of north east Ohio it had a problem starting, once it started it was ok. This started at approximately 2000 miles. I took it for service and it was hooked to the diagnostic computer. Upon return I was told that until the on board computer trips the service engine light there is nothing we can do for you. When it doesn't start at all, or the light comes on, bring it back. Handling was ok. Lots of engine noise. Six speed manual transmission was nice, but clutch plate made noise sometimes upon engagement.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is the first truck I can truly say meets ALL my needs and most of my wants.  It is large, roomy, comfortable and powerful.  With the diesel engine it doesn't even know a trailer is behind it even when the trailer is quite heavy. It is a pleasure to drive, though I do think the brakes are a bit spongy.  I would also be happier with a bit more mileage from the diesel engine.  All in all it is the best truck I have ever owned.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: We have been disappointed in the reliability of our truck. Our truck has 12,000 miles and has been in three dealerships due to major engine failures. The first was an out-of-place snap ring in a fuel injector, the second was foreign material that destroyed the oil pump gears, and the third is a major oil leak in the oil pump area. We have been surprised that two of the dealerships only had one diesel mechanic. We have been very upset that delivery of parts takes so long from Ford. We were stranded in another state and it took three days to get an oil pump for our truck. The 1-800 Ford hot line is a joke because you get no feedback or contacts. Once you buy a Ford truck all corporate contact disappears.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I ordered this truck for my construction business.  Ford did not let me down.  My last truck, a '92 F-150 lasted a long time.  If this one does the same, I will be well and truly pleased. The power of the 6.0 diesel has been phenomenal, however a bit more mileage wouldn't hurt at all.  The molded plastic steps make it VERY easy to get in and out of the tall truck.  On the minus side, there is an annoying clunk when the air-conditioning compressor kicks in, and this happens during the A/C cycle and the defrost cycle.  The dealer says it is normal. The brakes are a bit spongy, but will lock the tires if you press hard enough; it just takes some getting used to.  Overall, I am very satisfied.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I got my New tuck on my Wedding night! In front of all my friends and family. It was the best wedding gift ever. I loved too see that Ford came out with a Yellow Truck! Thanks for I love my     F-250 4X4 4 door Super Duty Yellow Truck. My new hubby has a F-350 2003 and he does not like his anymore, since I got mine! Got to love a girl and her truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Awesome truck. There is no equal.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This is my first big full size truck and I am truly enjoying the full power of the 6.0 diesel engine. It is smooth on the acceleration even when towing a 24 foot 5th wheel. Only have owned this vehicle for about two months but I already love the way it handles and the better than average fuel mileage for a large engine full size truck. con> The drivers seat could be more confortable, maybe it will get better with more wear. There is a clunk (sounds like the drive shaft) everytime I take of and make a left turn ... read that is normal for the F250HD Overall, I am very happy with this vehicle. It gives a quite ride, fairly good MPH, handles very will, my steering seems tight & true.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: I own a 03 F250 XLT FX4 Extended cab
Review: Iown the best truck for off road driving.I live on a dirt road and I'm about a mile in.My Ford has the plow package,I purchased a BOSS Plow with the help of fords $1,000 rebate and it plows my 11 hundred ft. driveway with ease.I live in NH,in the mountains on 10 acres so I cut and burn my own wood, and my F250 FX4 is a great help in that honey do list, [with the price of home heating oil]My Ford F250 FX4 is a big part of our family cause my wife loves the truck too,plenty of room for shopping

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab XLT Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: this truck makes an excellent tow vehicle but it handles like crap when not being used to tow or carry a load.Sometimes i feel like i'm drunk when i drive it,it;s all over the road.im hoping a new set of michelin tires will help i will keep you updated

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty SuperCab 4dr SuperCab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: the truck preforms great under loaded

column1: and highway driving. I pull a 29 ft.
5th wheel trailer the truck handles it
with great ease and doesn't lack for
power on flat land or mountain driving !

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: As of Dec 2011, I have owned this truck for over six years.It was bought new and I haven't experienced any problems during this ownership.The truck is used to pull a 24ft boat, large horse/cattle trailer, and utility trailer. Excellent interior space for front and rear passengers, more than ample pulling power, smooth transmission shifting, dashboard layout is exceptional, and multiple positions for rear seat storage/hauling/seating.As some posts mentioned gas mileage - a heavy duty truck was designed for pulling and hauling which makes gas mileage secondary. My next truck will definitely be an F-250 Lariat.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have owned since new and now have 106,000 miles and still have original tires (bfg rugged trail) and brakes still look factory new. A quirk here and there but I'm looking forward to hitting 500,000

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I waited years to buy my dream truck. The Ford F250 Diesel Super Duty Crew Cab. The last truck I would ever need to purchase. I just brought my truck in to the dealer, water pressure in the coolant reservoir. Service people with out looking under the hood told me what was wrong. The oil cooler and EGR cooler would need to be replaced. If not caught in time serious engine damage, head gaskets and worse $5,000 and worse. To all out there with a 6.0 diesel or thinking of buying one, consider the oil cooler a maintenance item at 50,000 miles. Have it replaced. From what I have read while learning whats wrong with my truck this is the major cause of problems on this engine. Pass it on

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Ford issued a recall for diesel emissions in late 2005, and blamed Ca Air Res Board for recall. NOT TRUE! Ford issued internal recall under state statute violation, and then recalibrated all 6.0 diesels. Performance dropped, turbos started blowing, mileage in the tank, continued issues with the EGR systems and oil leaks. THESE TRUCKS ARE TERRIBLE. I paid premium money for this truck, and am now in lemon law process and Ford is fighting me back and say nothing is wrong, but at the same time gave me 200K warranty on engine.. Yeah right. Piece of crap engine and NOT what I paid for and with this recall on problems they blame on CARB, as indicated by dealers, that is a flat out lie! Stay away!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I can say, first off, that I am satisfied with my truck for the most part. However, there are a lot of expensive parts, mainly the transmission, which sells new for around $7,000. I drove this truck for a little over a year and didn't have any trouble with it at all and when I finally did - it has been a huge ordeal since. The problem is that there doesn't seem to be anyone that has any knowledge of that style tranny. The main problem is that there are way too many electronic components, which makes it impossible for me to even work on without fear of making a small problem a huge catastrophe. Whatever happened to simplicity?

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Very comfortable and a fine looking truck whose handling is amazing for its size and weight. However with less then 65K miles the turbo has failed, the high pressure oil pump has failed, and the EGR cooler has leaked. The oil is always changed at 5000 miles (a must for this truck) and while the warranty has covered the repairs the trips to the dealer are tiresome

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XL 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Bought the truck new...shortly thereafter, when I would hit a bump at speed, the truck would lose steering, lose brakes, shake uncontrollably. make a sound like the end of the world. I took it in to be fixed. They claimed it was repaired 4 or 5 times!! Seriously dangerous stuff. I was bound to kill myself or someone else or whomever was driving it: my wife, mother, father-in-law. I spoke with Ford and got their TSBs...happens in a A LOT of the F250s(gas)! I asked to swap the truck out. No dice; they told me to Lemon Law it (Florida). I did...and won. Ford appealed the decision. This was about a year ago. We go trial (again) in January. When I win that case, Ford will appeal again

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: Best truck for carrying VIP passengers
Review: My 6L diesel truck has about 36k on it now, and never had an unscheduled maintenance. None of my many Toyotas were this reliable. I have always gotten around 14 to 16mpg in town (hills and stop signs and long, long red lights in Meridian, MS).  On the highway, I get over 23mpg if I am driving 55mph; as little as 18mpg if I am going 80 on a windy, rainy day, empty or loaded up and trailering. I have driven it in a hurricane (here, Katrina was all-day-long 45 to 55mph and the truck never felt unstable); my work can call me out at odd hours.  It seems as fast as my '06 Corvette, and is fine for 6 snooty adults!  Highly recommended!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I've driven this truck back and forth in Texas and enjoy every mile of it.  For a 10k lb truck, she drives like a dream.  I test drove the Dodge and Chevy, but neither one offered the room or options that I got with my Ford.  Haven't chipped it yet, but I am still getting 15-18 in city and 25 plus on the highway, as long as you stay out of the turbo and realize what you are driving and just kick back.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I found this vehicle excellent on the highway, comfort and acceleration is very good. I also found the truck to handle very nicely in town. Parking in a lot is a little difficult, but to be expected for a big truck. I have heard that Ford has a problem with this engine but this was not my experience. I am somewhat skeptical of buying another one because of the  "lemon" factor. BUT mine has been very good. I have driven the new 2007 King Ranch version like mine, very little difference.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I've had my diesel 4x4 truck for almost a year and thus far has given me perfect service...no problems whatsoever.  I often pull my enclosed car trailer (about 7500 lbs.) effortlessly. I get about 14 mpg around town, 18-19 mpg on the open road doing 80 mph and around 12 mpg when towing 65-70 mph.  I have the deluxe King Ranch model and is very comfortable.  I regularly get compliments about the truck when getting fuel.  The only thing that I would change would be not having the captain seats in the rear, but a bench seat for the sake of carrying groceries and packages inside.  I also like the availability of getting 16", 18", or 20" wheels, unlike GMC/GM were only 16" wheels are offered.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: After being stranded by 3 Chevys in a row I decided to try Ford. You will never be stuck or stranded with your horse trailer again! I have gone into cornfields with a 6 horse trailer and you put this baby in 4WD and no problem. Hills are a breeze when hauling horses and I'm in the Ozarks. It comes off the dealer lot READY TO PULL! Electrical is already set up. Interior is so luxurious that I hate to get in it in muddy boots. ROOMY! When not hitched to a trailer this truck is amazing to drive. This truck is FAST off the line and I say this as a 2002 Corvette owner. So much power make sure you have ballast in back when it snows. No problem towing in bad weather. A real beast of a truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD LB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I love my truck.  It fits me - I'm 6' 6" and I can wear a hat in the cab.  The machine drives well, is easy to maneuver and park. This is my fourth F250 diesel - all my others were the 7.3L engine. My experience with the 6.0L diesel is that it underperforms the 7.3L both in power and economy. I was used to 14.5-15.5 mpg city and 18-20 mpg highway with the 7.3L. The best I've gotten with the 6.0L is 13.0 city and 15.0 highway.  The 6.0L does not accelerate as well as the 7.3L did.  I'm disappointed, especially as the price of diesel has escalated out of sight.  There is a recall on the ECM and I hope that resolves the performance/economy problem.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I love this truck, it has a lot of power and rides like a car.  I just wish it would get better mpg.  I get about 14.5-15mpg around town.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XL 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I upgraded to from a '04 2wd F-250 to my '05 4wd.  What a difference in ride and turning radius night and day.  The 6.0 International Powerstroke is a pleasure to drive.  I can get 21 highway and 16 city.  I seldom go anywhere that someone doesn't comment on what a good looking truck it is.  I do not really haul anything or use it as a work truck, inside job, except for normal homeowner or occasional fire wood work but I have always wanted a 4wd diesel 4 door truck and this one will satisfy that desire for a long time.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Very nice to drive, very comfortable on long-distance treks. Great stereo, great performance from the motor. I have owned many trucks; this one has a real "truck" feel to it, (which is why I bought it), but is much more comfortable than any I have had before it.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: Great mileage for a large heavy truck
Review: I have the 6.0 Diesel; the '05 ride is totally different from '04. It's like my brother's GMC or my passenger car .  On the highway I get 20 miles per gallon and 13 to 16 in city depending on my foot. I love the power.  They've taken about 10 ft off the turn radius making it much easier to park, however it is a big truck and it's a dream to drive on the highway and freeway -- you see everything.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: Good truck, 5.4 powerful enough.  New 5 speed auto transmission was replaced at 5,000 miles.  Is starting to have the same problem (slipping) after less than 1,000 miles.  Dealer said some sort of ring broke.  The Lariat has great comfort features.  Power back sliding window, sunroof, seat heater.  Fuel economy stinks.  The trip computer says I've averaged 10.6 MPG.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: This has to be the most powerful truck I have ever owned.  Equipped with the Power Stroke Diesel this truck accelerates and handles better than most gas engines.  While towing a 25ft travel trailer it is easy to forget the trailer is still back there. When cruising at 65MPH and the tow haul mode set the engine is running right in its max torque range at about 1950 RPMs, while still averaging better fuel milage than my gas F-150 ever did.  Ford really got it right on this set up!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have only had this truck for a month and have put on 3000 miles. It is extreme yellow with the Amarillo black interior. 4X4 diesel. I get 17 + mph average. It is the nicest vehicle with plenty of room. The 4 door is really great. I drove truck over the road for 35 years and figured I deserved a new pick up. I traded an '03 F-150 which was ok but if you want a brute force truck this is it. I LOVE IT! Guess I over did this write up huh!

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I purchased my new F-250 with a Turbo-Diesel around April 2004.  I started having trouble after about 6,000 miles. The engine would just shut down to an idle.  You could not give it any fuel by the foot pedal.  I had it in the shop approximately six times from 6,000 miles to 11,000 miles.  It became very dangerous and unreliable.  It quit on my wife while crossing a railroad crossing. The dealership said after many times at their shop that the problem was a connection and they supposedly replaced the wiring loom for the accelerator. I finally became so disgusted that I traded it off for a Chevrolet Diesel. I enjoy it very much. I have heard a few others with the same problem I had. Ford needs to fix this.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I traded in a Cadillac STS for this truck. This is a different world. I look forward to getting up in the morning to drive this big truck. The speed bumps in my neighborhood are no longer huge obstacles for me to navigate. I've traded in some luxury and in return I got serious power. If John Wayne were alive, this is what he would drive.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review_Title: I Love My F-250 Crew Cab Truck!
Review: After owning a Silverado Ex-cab for 6 years I can't imagine why we didn't buy this sooner.  The F-250 Crew Cab diesel is so much fun to drive, has a huge interior space for the kids and all of our stuff, and it pulls our 27 foot camping trailer like it isn't even there!  Ford outdid themselves on this beautiful truck.  My Lincoln Towncar sits in the garage now that we have the F-250.  The kids love to ride to school in it, and they ask me to pick them up after school in the truck because they can hear me coming around the corner.  My husband flips up the rear seat and uses the back for extra cargo space, especially when it is raining.  Our whole family loves this truck.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I purchased this F 250 Diesel in early December of 2004.  I had read of the changes for 2005 a couple of years ago and decided to wait for the 2005 model. I am glad I did.  Ford made significant improvements over 2004.  The ride is significantly improved thanks to the coil springs up front rather than the old leaf springs.  Even for a diesel this vehicle is very quiet inside with no rattles.  The drivetrain is excellent with very smooth shifts.  The 5 speed Torq Shift transmission is highly recommended. I find the seats to be comfortable and the rear seat is much more roomy than my second choice, the Dodge Ram Crew.  The transmission and ride in the F 250 are better than the Dodge as well.

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat Rwd SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab Lariat 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: I have owned appx. 8 full size trucks since I began driving and by far this is the best riding, handling and certainly PARKING full size vehichle I've ever owned.To date I only have a couple thousand miles on the truck but I'm already impressed with the increased fuel mileage.This truck is equipped with a five speed automatic transmission and I'm currently averaging 16-17 miles per gallon around town I'm anxious to see how well it will do on a long trip.I've also been impressed with horsepower and tourque it feels far superior to the G.M "Duramax" diesel the ride is also much smoother.Ford has hit a homerun as far as I'm concerned with the new 2005 "Superduty"

Vehicle_Title: 2005 Ford F-250 Super Duty Crew Cab 4dr Crew Cab XLT 4WD SB (5.4L 8cyl 6M)
Review: The XLT Sport package is nice, but lacks the refinement that I was used in the F-150 Lariat. Also, the new 5.4L gas engine should not be used in this truck regardless of what the specs say. Based on the truck's weight and various observations, the V10 gas or Power Stroke diesel is the way to go. Horsepower is O.K., but something this heavy needs more torque. Overall, this is still a very nice truck. It rides pretty well and is capable of limited heavy duty requirements. Too bad it was not ordered with the V10!

The power from the 6.0 diesel is great. It turns heads everywhere I drive. Build quality is great, I have gone over the truck closely. All you guys in Louisville, GREAT JOB!!!!
